title: "Before the day"

  - /tracks/one-day-methods/before.html
---
Before the day you read the case study, the exercise overview and the first sections of the module on statistical methods, fit one model in the browser lab, and read the page on specification curves, which takes about two and a half hours. The day gives the causal graph, the estimators and the multiverse the time that the other formats give the tools and the practices of open research, and it assumes that a linear model and its output are not new to you. It is worked mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with the data already in place, so there is nothing that you have to install. Installing R, an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) and the downloadable workspace is optional and takes longer.

## 1. The case study

[Read the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The case study presents the original study, with its questions, data and selections, then SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses with an assessment of their choices, and how the results of the five analysts were put on one scale. Every part of the day works on this case.

## 2. The browser lab

[Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Open the lab once on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait until the R engine has loaded and the first cell shows a "Run Code" button, and run the three cells of Task 1. If they run, and the second reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years, you are set. If it does not load, try another browser, and tell the facilitator before the day.

## 3. The exercise

[Read the exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The exercise overview sets out the claim and the table of what the five Multi100 analysts found. Their recorded partial correlations run from −0.006 to −0.452, and working out how much of that spread comes from the analyses and how much from the conversion of their statistics takes up much of the day.

## 4. The statistics

[Read The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-aggregation){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Read sections 1 to 3 of the module, from [The country-year level](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-aggregation) to [Clustered standard errors](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-pooled). The sections say why the predictor is measured at the level of the country-year, read a first linear model output by output, and show what cluster-robust standard errors repair. Fit the first model yourself in an editable cell of the [browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-2-get-the-data-and-look-at-it).

## 5. Reading a specification curve

[Read Reading a specification curve](../../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The page prepares Part 4, on what a large set of results on the same data can and cannot establish together.

## 6. R and the workspace (optional)

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

If you want to work in your IDE, install R and an IDE, download the [workspace of the EU-frames case](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-workspace), and run `R/check_setup.R` until it reports no failure. Every fit of the menu then runs live on your machine. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met.

**By the start of the day** you have the browser lab loading on the machine that you will use, you have fitted one linear model on the panel and read its output, and you know how far apart the results of the five analysts are.
